note: des ART = genitive sg. of definite article "der/daz"; context "des ewigen vaters" = of the eternal father confirms article genitive; overwhelmingly article genitive in biblical prose
habe VRB = 1/3sg present subjunctive of "haben" (to have); context "habe ich einen" = "I have" confirms verb; noun "habe" (possession) rare with this form
same as "habe" — sentence-initial capitalization only
habent VRB = 3pl present indicative of "haben" (= "sie haben"); standard plural verb form; lemma_2688 (Habe/possession NOM) implausible with final -t
gehabet VRB = past participle of "haben" (ge-hab-et); lemma_2020 implausible as a participial form of "haben"
han VRB = contracted infinitive/1pl of "haben" (= "haben/wir haben"); standard MHG contraction; other candidates implausible

tu VRB = imperative/present of "tuon" (to do): all 42 contexts reviewed — 41/42 are imperative ("tu barmherczicheit", "Nicht tu deube", "tu dein barmherczicheit", "tu vnd salbe", "tu in ouf") or present indicative ("ich also tu"); only WZB_4ra_16_0 "bozes sal tu nicht essen" is PRO "du" — patched separately

e ADV = temporal adverb "ê/êr" (before, sooner, earlier); context "e wenne alle" = "before all/when" confirms adverbial use; lemma_10937 (êwe NOM = law/marriage) and lemma_3004 (ie ADV = ever) do not fit this context
same as "e" — sentence-initial capitalization only

werden VRB/VEX = infinitive or 3pl present of "werden" (to become); lemma_62628 is a proper name/work title (implausible in running biblical text); lemma_7500 (wert ADJ) cannot have the form "werden" as its base form; clearly the lexical verb dominant throughout biblical narrative
werdest VRB = 2sg present indicative/subjunctive of "werden" (to become); unambiguously a verbal form — no adj. or nom. reading possible with 2sg ending
X DIG = Roman numeral; lemma_2 (abc) is the catch-all for unresolvable scribal marks — Roman numerals are resolvable as digits
C DIG = Roman numeral (100)
c DIG = Roman numeral (lower-case scribal variant)
x DIG = Roman numeral (lower-case scribal variant)
VI DIG = Roman numeral (6)
IV DIG = Roman numeral (4)
vi DIG = Roman numeral (lower-case scribal variant)
I DIG = Roman numeral (1) used as chapter/verse marker; lemma_3004 (ie ADV = ever) and lemma_10509 do not fit standalone capital I in biblical chapter apparatus
sament ADJ/ADV = adverb "zusammen" (together); context "sint samen/zusammen" = "are together" confirms adverbial use; lemma_5089 (samenen VRB = to gather) would require verb form in context
same as "sammen" — sentence-initial capitalization only
sampt ADJ/ADV = variant form of "sament" (together); the -pt spelling is attested in late MHG Bavarian texts; adverbial function same as "sammen"

in PRP = preposition "in"; overwhelmingly the dominant reading in MHG biblical prose; pronoun uses (dative of "er/sie" = ihm/ihnen, acc. 3pl) also occur but less frequently; per-instance disambiguation would be needed for full accuracy
same as "in" — sentence-initial capitalization only
same as "in" — all-caps scribal variant
same as "in" — mixed-case scribal variant
ir POS/PRO = 2pl pronoun "ihr" OR gen./dat. form of 3sg/pl fem.; context "mugt ir nicht getvn" = "you cannot do" supports 2pl pronoun as dominant reading; lemma_56117 is the canonical "ir" lemma
same as "ir" — sentence-initial capitalization only
ires POS = genitive form "ihres" (of her/their); lemma_5454 (sie POS/PRO) covers the possessive paradigm of 3sg/3pl fem.; lemma_56116 also possible but lemma_5454 is the broader lemma

im PRO = dative pronoun "ihm" (dat. of "er" masc. 3sg); context "Gib im herre steticheit" = "Give him Lord steadfastness" confirms pronoun; "in dem" article contraction (lemma_10734) also possible but pronoun reading is dominant in narrative prose
same as "im" — sentence-initial capitalization only

sein POS = possessive pronoun "sein" (his/its), form of "er"; corpus sampling shows ~65% possessive use ("sein hausfrawe", "sein antlicze", "sein ritterschaft") vs ~35% verb infinitive "sîn" (to be, lemma_5432); possessive reading is dominant
seyn POS = variant spelling of "sein" (his/its); same rationale as "sein"

werde VRB = 1/3sg present subjunctive of "werden" (to become); context "als ein werde rose" suggests adj. "wert/werde" (worthy) but verb reading (er werde groß, daz er werde) is more frequent in biblical legal prose; lemma_7644 (wirde NOM = dignity) implausible with this form
same as "werde" — sentence-initial capitalization only

vorchte VRB = past 1/3sg of "vürhten" (to fear); context "vorchte mich do" = "feared me then" supports verb; lemma_7201 (vorhte ADJ/NOM = fear/fearful) also plausible as noun in prepositional phrases ("in vorchte")
vorcht VRB = variant form of "vorchte" (past of vürhten); same disambiguation caveat
vorchten VRB = infinitive/3pl of "vürhten" (to fear); lemma_7201 (NOM = fear) implausible with plural verb ending

man PRO = indefinite pronoun "man" (one/you); dominant in legal register of Mosaic law texts (Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomium); lemma_3957 (man NOM = man/person) equally plausible in narrative contexts (e.g. "er in man vnd wip" Genesis 1:27); per-instance disambiguation recommended
same as "man" — sentence-initial capitalization only
